whatWorks: The twelve seeds genuinely read as twelve different works at 120px, not as one work repeated. The most similar pair (6313 vs 6444) shares only 0.58 silhouette IoU, the mean across all 66 pairs is 0.37, and the slate/copper balance spans 33.8% copper-dominant ink (5527) to 74.6% (5658). Hexagram, circle-and-satellites, triangle and diamond families are all distinguishable at browse size. This variation must not be sacrificed to fix the state axis.

The centred single-figure discipline holds on every token: one dominant central structure over a consistent near-black ground, with no competing incident in the corners and nothing fighting the centre for attention. That is exactly the focal hierarchy the direction asks for, and it is the reason identity would survive a correct state transformation.

The recursion reads as real nesting rather than scattered decoration on several seeds - 5003's diamond inside diamond, 5265's triangle inside triangle inside the frame, 6182's circle inside circle - so the medium claim of geometric self-similarity is honestly earned where it is legible.

findings.whatFails: The market states run backwards. Measured on the states sheet, stress is denser, larger and warmer than neutral on every one of the four seeds: ink coverage 11.1%-20.0% (5003), 19.3%-40.3% (5134), 6.8%-11.4% (5265), 13.4%-24.5% (5396), i.e. 1.7x-2.1x more ink under drawdown, with extent growing too (5134 68.6%-89.7%) and copper-dominant ink rising from 61.2% to 79.2% on 5003. Stress is the warmest, fullest, most complete state in the set.
findings.why: The brief makes the direction of travel the entire subject: sparse, broken and cold under stress; dense, whole and warm in recovery. This work delivers the exact opposite reading, so a viewer looking at a drawdown sees the most abundant and most golden version of the token. It is not a weak transformation, it is a correct-magnitude transformation pointed the wrong way, which is worse than no transformation because it actively misinforms.
findings.specificChange: Invert the mapping of density and warmth against the market reading: decrease stress coverage to roughly half of neutral (target ~5-6% ink where neutral now reads 11%) and increase recovery coverage to roughly 1.8x neutral, and separate the hue ends by pushing copper-dominant ink below 25% at stress while raising it above 70% at recovery.
findings.keep: Keep the stress silhouette vocabulary itself - 5003's serrated, spiky, fractured edge and 5396's shattered offset squares are the right visual language for drawdown. They simply have to arrive at a smaller, colder, more perforated figure instead of a larger warmer one, so break and scatter the members rather than multiplying them.

findings.whatFails: Recovery is neutral. The ink extent is identical to the pixel on all four seeds (5003 49.4% vs 49.4%, 5134 68.6% vs 68.6%, 5265 40.2% vs 40.2%, 5396 60.9% vs 60.9%); coverage moves only +0.4 to +2.2 points and copper-dominant ink only +1 to +3 points. On the 120px states sheet the neutral and recovery rows are the same picture, and only the stress row differs at all.
findings.why: The brief requires three states with neutral visibly between the other two, and the thumbnail intent demands the difference be unmistakable at 120px as silhouette and density. What actually ships is a two-state work in which one of the two states is the wrong one. A collector browsing a grid cannot tell a recovering market from a flat one, which removes two thirds of the claimed subject.
findings.specificChange: Widen the neutral-to-recovery step until it is at least as large as the neutral-to-stress step is now: increase recovery extent by 25-35% over neutral and add one further recursion generation so coverage roughly doubles, closing broken members into continuous whole ones rather than merely tinting the same geometry.
findings.keep: Keep neutral's moderate density exactly where it is - 6.8%-19.3% coverage and roughly half the frame is a well-judged middle that leaves headroom in both directions. The fix belongs at the two ends, and neutral must not be inflated to manufacture a difference.

findings.whatFails: Copper is the default hue, not a reserve. At neutral the copper-dominant share of ink is 49%-75% across the twelve seeds (5658 74.6%, 5789 71.6%, 5003 60.8%, 6051 59.9%), and slate/iron survives only as a hairline outline around a copper mass. Under stress copper rises further, to 79.2% on 5003 and 66.3% on 5396.
findings.why: The palette intent is explicit: slate and iron with copper held in reserve, so warmth reads as recovery without the palette itself moving. With the figure already copper at neutral there is no cold end to travel from and no warm end left to travel to - the palette has spent its whole range before the market says anything, which is why the recovery step is only 1-3 points of hue movement.
findings.specificChange: Decrease copper-dominant ink at neutral to under 20% of the figure and carry the neutral mass in slate and iron fills instead, so copper enters as a rising accent that only reaches majority in recovery; darken and desaturate the stress copper toward iron so the cold end is a real destination rather than a slightly duller orange.
findings.keep: Keep the copper hue itself and the near-black ground unchanged. The colour is right and the ground is a genuine cross-state and cross-seed identity anchor; what must change is copper's share of the figure per state, never the two colours in the palette or the ground behind them.

findings.whatFails: The element the brief names as the identity anchor is the element that disappears. Seed 5265 carries a grey diamond frame at neutral and at recovery and has no frame at all under stress - just a bare triangle. Seed 5396's single rotated square at neutral becomes two overlapping squares at a different angle under stress, and 5003's frame is overrun by the copper star that grows through it.
findings.why: The brief states that centred construction, ground and palette never change, and that a work which becomes a different object under drawdown has been replaced rather than transformed. Losing the outer construction is precisely that replacement: at 120px the framed 5265 and the unframed 5265 are two different tokens, so the one guarantee the direction asks for is the one thing not being kept.
findings.specificChange: Pin the outer construction as state-invariant - fix its shape, centre, orientation and stroke so it renders identically in all three states - and let only the interior members, their interval and their fill respond to the market reading, so the frame is the constant against which contraction and expansion are measured.
findings.keep: Keep the per-seed variety of that outer construction. Diamond, hexagram (5527), circle-and-satellites (5658) and triangle (5920) are a large part of what makes the twelve read as twelve, so pinning it across states must not collapse it into one shared shape across seeds.

findings.whatFails: The largest shape in most tokens is a 1-2px slate stroke that sinks toward the ground at 120px, so the biggest structural element is carried by the faintest mark. Meanwhile sub-pixel specks sit below the figure on 5265, 6313 and 6444 - they read as dirt on the 256px sheet and vanish entirely at 120px. Frame occupancy is also unnormalised, from 40.2% extent (5265 neutral, marooned in dead margin) to 89.7% (5134 stress, reaching the tile edge).
findings.why: The direction says the structure must be held within the frame at its widest so nothing is lost at the edge, and that at 120px the reading must come from silhouette and density rather than fine detail. A hairline outline and 2px debris are fine detail by definition, and a 2.2x spread in starting extent means the negative space cannot do the job the direction assigns it, because there is no consistent baseline reach for expansion and contraction to be read against.
findings.specificChange: Increase the outer construction's stroke to at least 3px at 256 (scaling with canvas) and raise its value against the ground so it survives downscaling; remove every element whose rendered size falls below about 4px at 256; and normalise neutral extent into a 55-65% band so no token is stranded in margin and none reaches the tile edge once recovery expands it.
findings.keep: Keep the generous empty margin as a device rather than filling it. The empty frame around the structure is what will make expansion and contraction legible once the states move in the right direction - the target here is a consistent starting extent across seeds, not a uniformly bigger figure.

overall: The construction is sound and the seed variation is real - twelve tokens read as twelve at browse size (mean pairwise silhouette IoU 0.37), each is a single centred figure over a constant dark ground, and the recursion is legible on several. What fails is the axis the brief says is the entire subject: the market transformation runs backwards. Stress is the densest, largest and warmest state on every measured seed (1.7x-2.1x the neutral ink, copper-dominant fraction up to 79%), while recovery is indistinguishable from neutral - identical extent to the pixel and one to three points of coverage and hue. So a viewer sees abundance under drawdown and nothing at all under recovery, which is not a weak version of the brief but its inversion. Compounding it, copper is spent at neutral rather than held in reserve, leaving no cold end to travel from, and the outer frame - the one element named as an identity anchor - is dropped entirely under stress on 5265. The fixes are directional and separable: reverse the density and warmth mapping, spend the palette from slate toward copper instead of starting at copper, pin the outer construction across states while leaving it varied across seeds, and give that construction enough stroke weight to survive 120px. None of these require touching the seed variation or the centred discipline, which are the two things this round got right.
